findings.statement: CXCR2 is rank 1 in the convergence ranking: it is up in the biopsy meta-analysis, has genetic support in Open Targets and has clinical-stage antagonists (reparixin PHASE_3; navarixin, ladarixin, SX-682, elubrixin, danirixin PHASE_2; none labelled as UC-specific in the record). Expression meta-analysis [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.264]. Open Targets association score [gene=CXCR2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.5345].

CXCR2 sits in Reactome neutrophil degranulation, chemokine receptor-binding and G alpha(i) signalling, and its high-confidence STRING partners are the ELR+ chemokines CXCL8, CXCL1, CXCL5, CXCL2, CXCL6, CXCL3 and PPBP, plus CXCR1. This is a coherent neutrophil-recruitment axis (CXCR1/CXCR2 with CXCL8/CXCL1/CXCL5) that is up in the convergence ranking.

CXCL8 is strongly up in the biopsy meta-analysis and has anti-IL-8 antibodies in clinical development (ABX-IL8 and adakitug, PHASE_2), but it has no Open Targets genetic association signal, so its support is expression and literature rather than genetics. [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.704].

CHI3L1 is among the most strongly up genes in the biopsy meta-analysis, replicated in five cohorts, but has no genetic evidence and no approved or clinical drug (only predicted antibody and small-molecule tractability); it is better framed as a biomarker than a drug target. [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.714].

JAK2 is a genetically supported gene whose biopsy change is modest compared with the top expression-led genes (rank 33 in the convergence ranking). It has the second highest Open Targets association among known UC targets and approved or clinical JAK2 drugs for other indications (for example fedratinib, APPROVAL). Expression [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.872]. Association [gene=JAK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.7318].

IDO1 is strongly induced in UC mucosa and has IDO1 inhibitors in the clinic for other indications (epacadostat, linrodostat), but there is no Open Targets genetic association, so it is an expression-led, pharmacologically tractable candidate; the drugs are not UC-validated in the record. [gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.445].

OSMR combines up-regulation, genetic association and antibody tractability: vixarelimab (PHASE_2, anti-OSMR) is the only clinical drug, and the Reactome pathway is IL-6-type cytokine receptor ligand interactions. Expression [gene=OSMR; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.042]. Association [gene=OSMR; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.3907].

IL23A is a known UC target with rank 8 of 1999 in Open Targets association, yet it is not in the stored top of the convergence, target or biomarker rankings, so a genetically and clinically validated target is not a leading signal in the biopsy-based convergence score (the same holds for TNF). Convergence ranking therefore favours expression-led genes over validated targets.

CD274 (PD-L1) is up in UC biopsies and has genetic support in Open Targets; the anti-PD-L1 drugs listed (for example atezolizumab, sugemalimab) are oncology agents, so this is a mechanistic marker of immune checkpoint activation and not a treatment candidate for UC.

AQP9 is consistently up across cohorts and in inflamed vs non-inflamed mucosa, but it has no genetic evidence and no drug in Open Targets, so it is a biomarker candidate rather than a tractable target.

SLC26A2 is among the strongest down-regulated genes, which suggests epithelial or metabolic loss rather than an inflammatory gain. It has no genetic evidence and no drug, so it is not a drug-target candidate. [gene=SLC26A2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.496].

caveats: Only a subset of the top 40 genes had target profiles pulled (CXCR2, OSMR, CHI3L1) and one STRING query (CXCR2); other drug and tractability facts come from the convergence_ranking rows.
Open Targets drugs are listed for any indication; none of the listed drugs is shown to have UC efficacy in these records.
Open Targets association scores combine genetics, literature and other data types, so a nonzero overall score is not purely genetic.
IL23A and TNF were checked with gene_scores only (absent from stored top rankings); no biopsy log2fc was retrieved for them, so how they change in biopsies is not established here.
The PubMed connector needed authorization and was not used.
